Corollary 2.19 really prints this torsor group in v3 p. 13 and the journal p. 279. Independently checked Dolgachev, A brief introduction to Enriques surfaces, pp. 6–8: in characteristic zero Pic^0 is trivial and the canonical class generates Pic[2]. Over algebraically closed K, Kummer and proper GAGA give H^1_et(Y^an, μ_2) = Z/2, so the identity map of Pic^0 cannot be a torsor under that group. Use Pic^0[p]. Correct the proposed surjectivity repair: openness alone does not imply closedness for an analytic subgroup. Let P = Pic, G = P^0, N = P/G and Q = coker([p]:G→G) in étale sheaves. Proper base change makes the Kummer boundary constant on components, hence zero on G. The snake sequence then gives a surjection N[p] → Q; Lemma 2.21 makes G → Q constant, hence zero, so Q = 0. Fargues Lemmes 1/5 give étaleness and finiteness once surjectivity and the finite kernel are established. This repairs the proof without the unjustified open-subgroup argument; downstream finite étaleness survives.

Confirmed as a citation/hypothesis gap, not a disproof of the K-point conclusion. Theorem 3.20, v3 p. 22 and journal p. 293, assumes K-point surjectivity; HWZ v1/v2 Theorem 6.12 assumes local p-divisibility and its proof uses the analytic p-divisible identity component. The open subgroup V formed from the radius-one discs centred at K has V(K)=K but omits extension-valued points far from K; log is its inclusion into G_a. Thus the cited sheaf-surjectivity/local-p-divisibility criterion cannot be inferred from that K-point hypothesis. However V does have the asserted continuous K-point splitting (the identity), so it is not a counterexample to Theorem 3.20 itself. Extract the proven locally p-divisible version (or surjectivity as an étale sheaf), record the missing justification for the broader printed attribution, and observe that Theorems 3.2/3.22 supply the stronger hypothesis in both actual applications.
